question: By selling an article for ₹254.38, there is a gain of 10.6%. If it is sold for ₹224.25, then the loss/gain percentage will be :
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price = Rs.254.38

Gain % = 10.6% 

Final selling price = Rs.224.25

**Formula used:**

CP = SP/(100 + Gain%) × 100

Gain % = {(SP - CP)/CP} × 100

Loss % = {(CP - SP)/CP} × 100, where

CP = cost price

SP = selling price

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

Gain % = 10.6 = (254.38 - CP)/CP × 100

⇒ 10.6/100 = (254.38 - CP)/CP

⇒ CP × 0.106 = 254.38 - CP

⇒ 1.106 × CP = 254.38

⇒ CP = 254.38/1.106

⇒ CP = Rs.230

Now, final SP = 224.25

Loss % = {(CP - SP)/CP} × 100

Loss % = {(230 - 224.25)/230} × 100

⇒ (5.75/230) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 2.5%

**∴ If the article is sold for 224.25, then the loss % will be 2.5%.**
